units.leftText: Now the word of the LORD came to Jonah son of Amittai, saying,
units.rightText: Now the word of Jehovah came unto Jonah the son of Amittai, saying,

units.leftText: “Get up! Go to the great city of Nineveh and preach against it, because its wickedness has come up before Me.”
units.rightText: Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry against it; for their wickedness is come up before me.

units.leftText: Jonah, however, got up to flee to Tarshish, away from the presence of the LORD. He went down to Joppa and found a ship bound for Tarshish. So he paid the fare and went aboard to sail for Tarshish, away from the presence of the LORD. The Great Storm (Acts 27:13–26|ACT 27:13-26*)
units.rightText: But Jonah rose up to flee unto Tarshish from the presence of Jehovah; and he went down to Joppa, and found a ship going to Tarshish: so he paid the fare thereof, and went down into it, to go with them unto Tarshish from the presence of Jehovah.

units.leftText: Then the LORD hurled a great wind upon the sea, and such a violent storm arose that the ship was in danger of breaking apart.
units.rightText: But Jehovah sent out a great wind upon the sea, and there was a mighty tempest on the sea, so that the ship was like to be broken.

units.leftText: The sailors were afraid, and each cried out to his own god. And they threw the ship’s cargo into the sea to lighten the load. But Jonah had gone down to the lowest part of the vessel, where he lay down and fell into a deep sleep.
units.rightText: Then the mariners were afraid, and cried every man unto his god; and they cast forth the wares that were in the ship into the sea, to lighten it unto them. But Jonah was gone down into the innermost parts of the ship; and he lay, and was fast asleep.

units.leftText: The captain approached him and said, “How can you sleep? Get up and call upon your God. Perhaps this God will consider us, so that we may not perish.”
units.rightText: So the shipmaster came to him, and said unto him, What meanest thou, O sleeper? arise, call upon thy God, if so be that God will think upon us, that we perish not.

units.leftText: “Come!” said the sailors to one another. “Let us cast lots to find out who is responsible for this calamity that is upon us.” So they cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.
units.rightText: And they said every one to his fellow, Come, and let us cast lots, that we may know for whose cause this evil is upon us. So they cast lots, and the lot fell upon Jonah.

units.leftText: “Tell us now,” they demanded, “who is to blame for this calamity that is upon us? What is your occupation, and where have you come from? What is your country, and who are your people?”
units.rightText: Then said they unto him, Tell us, we pray thee, for whose cause this evil is upon us; what is thine occupation? and whence comest thou? what is thy country? and of what people art thou?

units.leftText: “I am a Hebrew,” replied Jonah. “I worship the LORD, the God of the heavens, who made the sea and the dry land.”
units.rightText: And he said unto them, I am a Hebrew; and I fear Jehovah, the God of heaven, who hath made the sea and the dry land.

units.leftText: Then the men were even more afraid and said to him, “What have you done?” The men knew that he was fleeing from the presence of the LORD, because he had told them. Jonah Cast into the Sea
units.rightText: Then were the men exceedingly afraid, and said unto him, What is this that thou hast done? For the men knew that he was fleeing from the presence of Jehovah, because he had told them.

units.leftText: Now the sea was growing worse and worse, so they said to Jonah, “What must we do to you to calm this sea for us?”
units.rightText: Then said they unto him, What shall we do unto thee, that the sea may be calm unto us? for the sea grew more and more tempestuous.

units.leftText: “Pick me up,” he answered, “and cast me into the sea, so it may quiet down for you. For I know that I am to blame for this violent storm that has come upon you.”
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Take me up, and cast me forth into the sea; so shall the sea be calm unto you: for I know that for my sake this great tempest is upon you.

units.leftText: Nevertheless, the men rowed hard to get back to dry land, but they could not, for the sea was raging against them more and more.
units.rightText: Nevertheless the men rowed hard to get them back to the land; but they could not: for the sea grew more and more tempestuous against them.

units.leftText: So they cried out to the LORD: “Please, O LORD, do not let us perish on account of this man’s life! Do not charge us with innocent blood! For You, O LORD, have done as You pleased.”
units.rightText: Wherefore they cried unto Jehovah, and said, We beseech thee, O Jehovah, we beseech thee, let us not perish for this man’s life, and lay not upon us innocent blood; for thou, O Jehovah, hast done as it pleased thee.

units.leftText: Then they picked up Jonah and cast him into the sea, and the raging sea grew calm.
units.rightText: So they took up Jonah, and cast him forth into the sea; and the sea ceased from its raging.

units.leftText: Then the men feared the LORD greatly, and they offered a sacrifice to the LORD and made vows to Him.
units.rightText: Then the men feared Jehovah exceedingly; and they offered a sacrifice unto Jehovah, and made vows.

units.leftText: Now the LORD had appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah spent three days and three nights in the belly of the fish.
units.rightText: And Jehovah prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah; and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.

units.leftText: From inside the fish, Jonah prayed to the LORD his God,
units.rightText: Then Jonah prayed unto Jehovah his God out of the fish’s belly.

units.leftText: saying: “In my distress I called to the LORD, and He answered me. From the belly of Sheol I called for help, and You heard my voice.
units.rightText: And he said, I called by reason of mine affliction unto Jehovah, And he answered me; Out of the belly of Sheol cried I, And thou heardest my voice.

units.leftText: For You cast me into the deep, into the heart of the seas, and the current swirled about me; all Your breakers and waves swept over me.
units.rightText: For thou didst cast me into the depth, in the heart of the seas, And the flood was round about me; All thy waves and thy billows passed over me.

units.leftText: At this, I said, ‘I have been banished from Your sight; yet I will look once more toward Your holy temple.’
units.rightText: And I said, I am cast out from before thine eyes; Yet I will look again toward thy holy temple.

units.leftText: The waters engulfed me to take my life; the watery depths closed around me; the seaweed wrapped around my head.
units.rightText: The waters compassed me about, even to the soul; The deep was round about me; The weeds were wrapped about my head.

units.leftText: To the roots of the mountains I descended; the earth beneath me barred me in forever! But You raised my life from the pit, O LORD my God!
units.rightText: I went down to the bottoms of the mountains; The earth with its bars closed upon me for ever: Yet hast thou brought up my life from the pit, O Jehovah my God.

units.leftText: As my life was fading away, I remembered the LORD. My prayer went up to You, to Your holy temple.
units.rightText: When my soul fainted within me, I remembered Jehovah; And my prayer came in unto thee, into thy holy temple.

units.leftText: Those who cling to worthless idols forsake His loving devotion.
units.rightText: They that regard lying vanities Forsake their own mercy.
leftNotes: 2:8 Forms of the Hebrew chesed are translated here and in most cases throughout the Scriptures as loving devotion; the range of meaning includes love, goodness, kindness, faithfulness, and mercy, as well as loyalty to a covenant.

units.leftText: But I, with the voice of thanksgiving, will sacrifice to You. I will fulfill what I have vowed. Salvation is from the LORD!”
units.rightText: But I will sacrifice unto thee with the voice of thanksgiving; I will pay that which I have vowed. Salvation is of Jehovah.

units.leftText: And the LORD commanded the fish, and it vomited Jonah onto dry land.
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto the fish, and it vomited out Jonah upon the dry land.

units.leftText: Then the word of the LORD came to Jonah a second time:
units.rightText: And the word of Jehovah came unto Jonah the second time, saying,

units.leftText: “Get up! Go to the great city of Nineveh and proclaim to it the message that I give you.”
units.rightText: Arise, go unto Nineveh, that great city, and preach unto it the preaching that I bid thee.

units.leftText: This time Jonah got up and went to Nineveh, in accordance with the word of the LORD.
units.rightText: So Jonah arose, and went unto Nineveh, according to the word of Jehovah. Now Nineveh was an exceeding great city, of three days’ journey.

units.leftText: On the first day of his journey, Jonah set out into the city and proclaimed, “Forty more days and Nineveh will be overturned!”
units.rightText: And Jonah began to enter into the city a day’s journey, and he cried, and said, Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown.

units.leftText: And the Ninevites believed God. They proclaimed a fast and dressed in sackcloth, from the greatest of them to the least.
units.rightText: And the people of Nineveh believed God; and they proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them even to the least of them.

units.leftText: When word reached the king of Nineveh, he got up from his throne, took off his royal robe, covered himself with sackcloth, and sat in ashes.
units.rightText: And the tidings reached the king of Nineveh, and he arose from his throne, and laid his robe from him, and covered him with sackcloth, and sat in ashes.

units.leftText: Then he issued a proclamation in Nineveh: “By the decree of the king and his nobles:
units.rightText: And he made proclamation and published through Nineveh by the decree of the king and his nobles, saying, Let neither man nor beast, herd nor flock, taste anything; let them not feed, nor drink water;

units.leftText: Furthermore, let both man and beast be covered with sackcloth, and have everyone call out earnestly to God. Let each one turn from his evil ways and from the violence in his hands.
units.rightText: but let them be covered with sackcloth, both man and beast, and let them cry mightily unto God: yea, let them turn every one from his evil way, and from the violence that is in his hands.

units.leftText: Who knows? God may turn and relent; He may turn from His fierce anger, so that we will not perish.”
units.rightText: Who knoweth whether God will not turn and repent, and turn away from his fierce anger, that we perish not?

units.leftText: When God saw their actions— that they had turned from their evil ways— He relented from the disaster He had threatened to bring upon them.
units.rightText: And God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God repented of the evil which he said he would do unto them; and he did it not.

units.leftText: Jonah, however, was greatly displeased, and he became angry.
units.rightText: But it displeased Jonah exceedingly, and he was angry.
leftNotes: 4:1 Or It was exceedingly evil to Jonah, and he became angry

units.leftText: So he prayed to the LORD, saying, “O LORD, is this not what I said while I was still in my own country? This is why I was so quick to flee toward Tarshish. I knew that You are a gracious and compassionate God, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion — One who relents from sending disaster.
units.rightText: And he prayed unto Jehovah, and said, I pray thee, O Jehovah, was not this my saying, when I was yet in my country? Therefore I hasted to flee unto Tarshish; for I knew that thou art a gracious God, and merciful, slow to anger, and abundant in lovingkindness, and repentest thee of the evil.

units.leftText: And now, O LORD, please take my life from me, for it is better for me to die than to live.”
units.rightText: Therefore now, O Jehovah, take, I beseech thee, my life from me; for it is better for me to die than to live.

units.leftText: But the LORD replied, “Have you any right to be angry?”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said, Doest thou well to be angry?

units.leftText: Then Jonah left the city and sat down east of it, where he made himself a shelter and sat in its shade to see what would happen to the city.
units.rightText: Then Jonah went out of the city, and sat on the east side of the city, and there made him a booth, and sat under it in the shade, till he might see what would become of the city.

units.leftText: So the LORD God appointed a vine, and it grew up to provide shade over Jonah’s head to ease his discomfort, and Jonah was greatly pleased with the plant.
units.rightText: And Jehovah God prepared a gourd, and made it to come up over Jonah, that it might be a shade over his head, to deliver him from his evil case. So Jonah was exceeding glad because of the gourd.
leftNotes: 4:6 Hebrew qiqayon; that is, possibly the castor oil plant; also in verses 7, 9, and 10

units.leftText: When dawn came the next day, God appointed a worm that attacked the plant so that it withered.
units.rightText: But God prepared a worm when the morning rose the next day, and it smote the gourd, that it withered.

units.leftText: As the sun was rising, God appointed a scorching east wind, and the sun beat down on Jonah’s head so that he grew faint and wished to die, saying, “It is better for me to die than to live.”
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when the sun arose, that God prepared a sultry east wind; and the sun beat upon the head of Jonah, that he fainted, and requested for himself that he might die, and said, It is better for me to die than to live.

units.leftText: Then God asked Jonah, “Have you any right to be angry about the plant?” “I do,” he replied. “I am angry enough to die!”
units.rightText: And God said to Jonah, Doest thou well to be angry for the gourd? And he said, I do well to be angry, even unto death.

units.leftText: But the LORD said, “You cared about the plant, which you neither tended nor made grow. It sprang up in a night and perished in a night.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said, Thou hast had regard for the gourd, for which thou hast not labored, neither madest it grow; which came up in a night, and perished in a night:

units.leftText: So should I not care about the great city of Nineveh, which has more than 120,000 people who cannot tell their right hand from their left, and many cattle as well?”
units.rightText: and should not I have regard for Nineveh, that great city, wherein are more than sixscore thousand persons that cannot discern between their right hand and their left hand; and also much cattle?
